results.title: Bank Mandiri Issues USD750 Million Perpetual Bond to Strengthen Capital
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk. issued a USD750 million perpetual bond on September 10, 2026, as Additional Tier 1 capital to strengthen its capital structure. The bond carries an initial distribution rate of 7.35% per year and was offered to investors outside the United States under Regulation S, with listing on the Singapore Exchange. Proceeds will be used to reinforce the bank's capital position in accordance with OJK Regulation No. 11/POJK.03/2016. The issuance, arranged by HSBC, J.P. Morgan Securities, Mandiri Securities, and Standard Chartered Bank, falls below the 20% equity threshold and does not constitute a material transaction under OJK Regulation No. 17/POJK.04/2020.

results.title: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signs Master Restructuring Agreement to restructure Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state-owned banks
results.body: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signed a Master Restructuring Agreement on 10 September 2026 to restructure its Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state‑owned banks. The debt is divided into three tranches: Tranche A of about Rp13.33 trillion at 3.5% per year (1% cash quarterly and 2.5% deferred to 2041) to be repaid over 15 years via a balloon payment; Tranche B of about Rp4.05 trillion at 1% per year with a five‑year bullet payment funded by divestment proceeds; and Tranche C covering accrued interest from the standstill period, repaid in interest‑free installments over 18 months. The participating lenders are PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (acting as Facility Agent), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. Certain working‑capital facilities tied to project owners are excluded from the restructuring and will be serviced independently of project cash flows.

results.title: PTPP Restructures Rp18.2 Trillion Debt, Detailing Payment Schemes
results.body: PT PP (Persero) Tbk (PTPP) has restructured Rp18.2 trillion of debt into three tranches: Tranche A (Rp13.33 trillion) with a 15‑year balloon payment and 3.5% interest, Tranche B (Rp4.05 trillion) with a five‑year bullet payment and 1% interest, and Tranche C covering interest or profit‑share accrued since the stand‑still, paid over 18 months. The restructuring, governed by a Master Restructuring Agreement signed on 10 September 2026 with PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, will take effect after a shareholders’ meeting. PTPP aims to transform its business and finances to sustain operations, improve performance, and repay creditors. The agreement also excludes certain working‑capital facilities, which remain independent of project cash flows.

results.title: PT PP Tbk signs Rp18.2 trillion debt restructuring agreement with four state‑owned banks
results.body: PT PP Tbk entered into a Master Restructuring Agreement on 10 September 2026 to restructure Rp18.2 trillion of debt with four state‑owned banks. The agreement, in which PT Bank Mandiri Tbk acts as the facility agent and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk serve as lenders, splits the debt into Tranche A of about Rp13.33 trillion at 3.5% annual interest (1% cash quarterly, 2.5% deferred to 2041), Tranche B of about Rp4.05 trillion at 1% annual interest with bullet repayment over five years, and Tranche C covering interest accrued from the stand‑still period with interest‑free repayments over 18 months. Repayment of Tranche A will be made over 15 years with a balloon payment, while Tranche B’s repayment is sourced from divestments, and Tranche C’s installments are independent of project cash flows. The restructuring becomes effective after the shareholders’ meeting and fulfillment of the conditions set out in the MRA, and is intended to support PT PP’s business and financial transformation and ensure its ability to service all creditors.

results.title: PT Rukun Raharja Tbk (RAJA) posts 102% net profit surge to US$15.54 million in H1-2026 on bargain purchase gain from Madura Block acquisition
results.body: PT Rukun Raharja Tbk (RAJA) reported a 102% year-on-year increase in net profit to US$15.54 million for the first half of 2026, driven primarily by a bargain purchase gain from the acquisition of SMSD Development, which includes a 20% stake in Husky-CNOOC Madura Limited (HCML). Revenue rose 2% to US$25.65 million supported by stable lifting at the Jabung Block and higher oil prices, while adjusted EBITDA grew 38% to US$21.28 million. The acquisition was financed through bond issuance and a Bank Mandiri loan, pushing total assets to US$231.8 million and liabilities to US$166.8 million, with the debt-to-equity ratio rising to 2.42 times but remaining below covenant limits of 5 times for bonds and 4 times for Raharja Energi Madura. Net profit margin reached 66.61% and return on equity hit 47.8%.

results.title: Bank Mandiri Completes USD 750 Million Perpetual Bond Issuance at 7.35%
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk completed the issuance of a USD 750 million Additional Tier 1 perpetual bond with an initial distribution rate of 7.35% on 10 September 2026. The bond was offered to investors outside the United States under Regulation S and listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange, with HSBC, J.P. Morgan Securities, Mandiri Securities, and Standard Chartered Bank acting as joint lead managers. Proceeds will strengthen the bank's capital structure and the issuance is not classified as a material transaction as it represents less than 20% of equity based on the 30 June 2026 audited financial statements. As of that date, the bank's consolidated Tier 1 capital stood at Rp249.16 trillion, Tier 2 capital at Rp17.08 trillion, and total capital at Rp266.25 trillion, all lower than the same period in 2025.

results.title: Assessing PT Bank Mandiri Tbk Stock Prospects After the Interim Dividend of Rp6.16 Trillion
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk's stock prospects are discussed after the bank announced an interim dividend of Rp6.16 trillion (Rp66 per share). The dividend is cited as a sign of solid profitability, with net profit of Rp37.5 trillion, up 22.3% year‑on‑year to August 2026, and credit disbursements growing 17.6% YoY to Rp1,592 trillion. Total assets increased 20.7% YoY to Rp2,358 trillion, and the gross non‑performing loan ratio remained at 1%. The interim payout is part of a total 2026 dividend distribution of Rp50.63 trillion (Rp542.95 per share), indicating ample capital capacity to support continued credit expansion.

results.title: Commissioner Yuliot buys 22,800 Bank Mandiri shares ahead of interim dividend
results.body: Bank Mandiri commissioner Yuliot purchased 22,800 Bank Mandiri shares on 7 September 2026 at an execution price of Rp4,380 per share, costing roughly Rp99.86 million. The transaction raised Yuliot’s total holding to 188.4 thousand shares, representing about 0,0001 % of the bank’s equity. The purchase appears aimed at capturing the interim dividend that Bank Mandiri plans to distribute at Rp66 per share, for an estimated total payout of Rp6.16 trillion, with cum‑dividend regular market and negotiation on 15 September 2026, ex‑dividend regular market and negotiation on 16 September 2026, cum‑dividend cash market on 17 September 2026, ex‑dividend cash market on 18 September 2026, and payment on 2 October 2026. Bank Mandiri’s interim dividend is based on its 30 June 2026 financials, which reported a net profit of Rp30.41 trillion, retained earnings of Rp211.84 trillion, and total accumulated equity of Rp293.02 trillion.

results.title: Yuliot, Ir buy Shares of Bank Mandiri
results.body: Bank Mandiri insider Ir. Yuliot purchased 22,800 shares at IDR 4,380 each on Sep 7, 2026, costing IDR 99,864,000 and raising his holding to 188,400 shares, still below 0.001% of the float. The buy follows earlier purchases of 101,700 shares on July 30 at IDR 4,120 and 22,400 shares on Sep 8 at IDR 4,430, reflecting continued accumulation by the insider.

results.title: Yuliot, Ir Buy Shares of Bank Mandiri
results.body: Insider Yuliot, Ir purchased 22,400 Bank Mandiri shares at IDR 4,430 per share on 2026-09-04, totaling IDR 99,232,000. The acquisition increased his holding from 143,200 to 165,600 shares, with ownership remaining at 0.000% of the company, and was made for investment purposes.

results.title: Stock picks for weak IHSG: index falls 0.25% on foreign selling, DMAS pre-sales at 55% target, MPXL eyes barge expansion, BMRI sets Rp66 interim dividend
results.body: The article provides a market wrap and stock ideas as the IHSG slipped 0.25% to 6,619.67 on Monday, driven by foreign net selling of Rp678.54 billion across the market. Six of eleven sectors weakened, led by financials down 0.76%, while industrials rose 1.25% and healthcare gained 0.82% on moves in MEDS, DKHH, KAEF, HALO, SOHO, and IRRA. DMAS reported first-half pre-sales of Rp1.15 trillion, reaching 55% of its Rp2.08 trillion annual target, with data-center demand driving 64 hectares of the 85 hectares of industrial land sold, prompting consideration of converting commercial and residential land. MPXL posted a 28.8% revenue increase to Rp73.12 billion in the first half, aims to start barge-based coal transport in 2027 via PT Tambang Raya Sejahtera, but faces RKAB restrictions at mines in South Sumatra and Kalimantan. Bank Mandiri (BMRI) declared an interim dividend of Rp66 per share, totalling approximately Rp6.16 trillion and representing a 20.26% payout ratio on first-half net profit, with cum date 15 September 2026 and payment 2 October 2026.

results.title: IHSG forecast to reach 6,700 amid Anak Krakatau eruption concerns, with BBCA, BBRI, BMRI under pressure and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommending IMPC, TINS, KOTA, UDNG.
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) could climb to the 6,600‑6,700 range, with a key resistance at 6,700, despite the ongoing Anak Krakatau eruption. On Monday the index slipped 0.25% to 6,619.67, staying above the 20‑day moving average and with a positive MACD, while foreign‑exchange reserves rose to US$146.5 billion supporting domestic sentiment. Technical pressure is coming from BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, whereas BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends swing‑trade positions in IMPC and TINS, a day‑trade in KOTA, and a sell stance on UDNG. The market’s near‑term direction may be swayed by the U.S. CPI release on 11 September, projected at 3.4% headline and 2.4% core inflation, which could affect risk appetite and the index’s trajectory.

results.title: Foreign Investor Outflow Rp590 Billion, Two Prajogo Pangestu‑Affiliated Stocks Lead Net Sell
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net outflow of Rp590.18 billion on Monday, with the market turning to net sell positions. The top net‑sell stocks were PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp121.2 billion, 61.03 million shares) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (Rp87.9 billion, 93.60 million shares), followed by PT Indosat Tbk (Rp64.8 billion, 27.53 million shares), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (Rp62.3 billion, 77.91 million shares) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp53.7 billion, 12.21 million shares); the two leading losers are affiliated with Prajogo Pangestu. On the buy side, PT Bumi Resources Tbk led with a net buy of Rp180.5 billion and 830 million shares, while PT Bukit Asam Tbk, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk, PT MNC Energy Investments Tbk and PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk recorded net buys of Rp52.2 billion, Rp38.1 billion, Rp31.6 billion and Rp27.2 billion respectively, with volumes of 173.9 million, 3.26 million, 230 million and 130 million shares.

results.title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk announces interim dividend of Rp 66 per share for FY 2026
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk announced an interim dividend of Rp 66 per share for fiscal year 2026, amounting to a total payout of Rp 6.16 trillion. The dividend was approved by the Board of Directors on 3 September 2026 and disclosed on 7 September 2026, using financial data as of 30 June 2026. The payment schedule includes regular and negotiated market distribution on 15‑16 September, cash market distribution on 17‑18 September, and the record date set for 17 September at 16:00 WIB. PT Bank Mandiri Tbk reported a net profit attributable to the parent of Rp 30.41 trillion for the first half of 2026, retained earnings of Rp 211.84 trillion, and total equity of Rp 293.02 trillion.

results.title: Bank Mandiri Announces Interim Dividend of Rp 6.16 Trillion, Total Dividend for 2026 Reaches Rp 50.63 Trillion
results.body: Bank Mandiri Tbk announced an interim dividend of Rp 66 per share, totaling Rp 6.16 trillion, bringing its cumulative dividend for 2026 to Rp 50.63 trillion. The announcement follows a 2025 dividend of Rp 44.47 trillion and reflects the bank’s confidence in its fundamentals, supported by a 22.3% YoY increase in net profit to Rp 37.5 trillion and a 20.7% YoY rise in total assets to Rp 2,358 trillion. Credit disbursements grew 17.6% YoY to Rp 1,592 trillion, backed by a 17.6% YoY rise in third‑party funding to Rp 1,687 trillion, while the gross NPL ratio remained at 1.00%. The dividend will be paid to shareholders recorded on the ex‑dividend dates set for September and October 2026.

results.title: IHSG Projected to Remain Limited on Tuesday (Sept 8), Sentiment Overview
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) is projected to trade within a limited range on Tuesday (Sept 8) after closing at 6,619.67, down 16.80 points (0.25%) on Monday, with analysts noting pressure from big‑cap financial stocks BBCA, BBRI and BMRI while health and energy sectors provide support and technical levels suggest support near 6,603‑6,600 and resistance near 6,632‑6,700. Analysts from MNC Sekuritas and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas set target prices for HRUM (Rp 985‑1,015), INKP (Rp 9,250‑9,500), MDKA (Rp 2,980‑3,020) and recommend buying IMPC (Rp 1,605‑1,730), TINS (Rp 4,610‑4,830) and KOTA (Rp 224‑236) as the market watches upcoming NFP, China trade‑balance and US CPI releases and Indonesia’s foreign‑exchange reserves at US$146.5 billion.

results.title: Lending to state-owned enterprises remains a key driver of credit growth for Indonesia's state-owned banks, with Bank Mandiri, BNI, and BSI reporting double-digit expansion in the first half of 2026.
results.body: LPPI Senior Vice President Trioksa Siahaan said credit to BUMN continues to be a primary growth engine for Himbara banks, particularly for infrastructure, energy, and strategic projects, while warning that concentration risk requires internal limits, syndication, and risk sharing beyond regulatory caps. Bank Mandiri channeled Rp489 trillion to the government and BUMN ecosystem as of June 2026, up 41.6% year-on-year, with a 0.98% NPL ratio and 242% coverage. BNI's lending to BUMN surged 63.2% to Rp197.8 trillion, with the bank emphasizing prudent management amid infrastructure debt extension issues. BSI's total financing grew 15.98% to Rp340.09 trillion, lifting its market share to 3.75%, driven by corporate lending growth of 21.13% and SME growth of 19.98%, with BUMN exposure spread across wholesale and retail segments.

results.title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
results.body: Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

results.title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk announces interim dividend of Rp66 per share, payable on 2 October 2026
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk disclosed that it will distribute an interim dividend of Rp66 per share for the 2026 fiscal year. The dividend was approved by the Board of Commissioners on 3 September 2026 and announced on 7 September 2026. Shareholders recorded in the KSEI system as of the record date on 17 September 2026 will receive the payment on 2 October 2026, with cum‑dividend dates set for 15 September (regular and negotiation markets) and 17 September (cash market) and ex‑dividend dates on 16 September and 18 September respectively. The distribution follows the provisions of Indonesian corporate law, the Bursa Efek Indonesia rules on interim dividends, and the company’s articles of association.

results.title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk announces Rp 6.16 trillion interim dividend for FY 2026
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk announced an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026 totaling Rp 6.16 trillion, or Rp 66 per share. The dividend schedule sets cum‑dividend on 15 September 2026, ex‑dividend on 16 September 2026, record date on 17 September 2026, and payment on 2 October 2026. The payout is based on financial data as of 30 June 2026, when the bank reported net profit attributable to the parent of Rp 30.41 trillion, retained earnings of Rp 211.84 trillion, and total equity of Rp 293.02 trillion. The announcement was disclosed by the corporate secretary Bank Mandiri Adhika Vista following board approval on 3 September 2026.
